report.summary: Reviewed the four supplied files only (lib/first-use-guide.ts, app/components/FirstUseGuide.tsx, tests/first-use-guide.test.ts, and the proofbeforepay-delivery skill). The previous fixes are in the source: exportFirstUseGuide derives endedAt from value.lastMono (the real stop of the last task) where lastMono is set in finishGuideTask, and the separate download clock only checks finite and non-rollback (lines 32 and 31). Every session exports mode 'operator_walkthrough' with unfamiliarWithProject false, externalParticipant false and consent not_requested (line 33). Refusal and ordering help are present: incomplete sessions refuse export with GUIDE_INCOMPLETE (line 32), a blocked or abandoned outcome without a reason is refused (line 21), the 20-help cap label is explicit (line 18), and the blocked-vs-abandoned explanation and reason label are present (line 19). No reachable P1 or P2 defect was found in these files. One concrete P3 UI label defect is reported: the 3/3 status is hard-coded for both personas, and it is inconsistent because the technical_seller persona has a different number of tasks. Checks were not run; the test file and the shared validator first-use-session.mjs were not supplied, so its field rules remain unverified here.

findings.title: Task progress status always says "/3" even when the persona has a different task count
findings.evidence: Line 17 renders `已记录 ${run.tasks.length}/3 项` / `Recorded ${run.tasks.length}/3 tasks` with the denominator hard-coded to 3. The same file supports two personas: line 16 offers 'technical_seller', and beginGuideTask (lib/first-use-guide.ts:14-15) takes the next task id from `TASKS[value.persona]`, which can have a different length. The completion logic in FirstUseGuide.tsx line 22 and exportFirstUseGuide line 32 compares against `TASKS[value.persona].length`, not 3. The UI therefore reports task progress that disagrees with the library's real sequence length whenever technical_seller's TASKS array is not 3 long.
findings.reproduction: Not executed (no runtime or test run requested). Reasoning trace: create a guide with persona 'technical_seller' (line 16) and call beginGuideTask three times while finishing each task. If TASKS.technical_seller has length N (for example 2), then after 2 finished tasks line 17 shows '2/3', even though line 22 already offers download because run.tasks.length===N and !active. The user sees an incomplete count while the record is actually complete, or a misleading denominator. Only source was checked; the length of TASKS.technical_seller is not in the packet and is a limitation.
findings.suggestion: Use the persona's real task count instead of the literal 3, for example add `const total=TASKS[persona].length` (imported or exposed from first-use-session.mjs, as the library already uses it) and render `${run.tasks.length}/${total}`, and use the same `total` for the line 22 completion condition.

limitations: Only the four supplied files were read. lib/first-use-session.mjs, the TASKS definition, first-use-guide.css, app files that use the component, and README were not in the packet, so the validator's strict field rules, the actual TASKS lengths and how the component is wired were not checked.
No code executed. "17 tests green" is reported by the requester and was not verified; the one reproduction is a source-based reasoning trace.

Whether TASKS.technical_seller.length differs from 3 cannot be confirmed from the packet, so the P3 is conditional on that. It is concrete only in the sense that the label and the library's completion check use different sources for the same count.
Privacy, timing, order and help-refusal boundaries were checked in the supplied source and no reachable P1/P2 was found. This is not a claim that the shared validator enforces the same limits.

No judgment on whether a non-root participant took part: the UI copy and export treat every session as operator walkthrough, as the requester described, and this packet cannot establish or rule that out.
Business actions (acceptance, payment, membership) are not triggered in the supplied UI: there is no call to them, but the surrounding app was not supplied.
